function: Active sensing: GRUs and DNNs design ping-pong pilot beamformers, then precoder and combiner for multi-stream TDD MIMO, fully digital and hybrid, without channel estimation (pp. 1, 5-7).
system: Point-to-point TDD MIMO, block fading: 64x64 fully digital, 64x16 ray tracing at 3.5 GHz, hybrid 64x64 with 8 RF chains (mmWave); no RIS (pp. 3, 7-8, 12).
method: GRU cells plus fully connected DNNs unrolled over L pilot rounds with QR power-iteration step; unsupervised end-to-end training on the log-det objective, offline (pp. 5-7, 11-12).
data_channel: Rayleigh i.i.d. CN(0,1) channels; Sionna ray tracing at 3.5 GHz (64x16); sparse mmWave geometric model, Lp=4 or 10 paths; 1000 random test channels (pp. 7-8, 12).
test_conditions: Same channel family for training and testing; Rayleigh-trained model also tested on ray-tracing data; model trained at L=8 rounds tested at other L (pp. 7-9).
baselines: LMMSE+SVD, power iteration [7], summed power [20] (digital); SVD with perfect CSI, power iteration with codebook [26], OMP+SVD [10], MTQR [24] (hybrid); no learned baseline (pp. 7, 13).
metrics: Average beamforming objective log-det vs. SNR and pilot length, achievable rate, correlation with true singular vectors, CPU/GPU inference time (pp. 7-8, 14-15).
complexity: Inference time for 128x32 digital MIMO: proposed 0.9079 ms CPU, 0.0348 ms GPU vs 0.0230 to 0.3901 ms for benchmarks (Table I, p. 15).
q1_support: p. 8: "a ray-tracing based channel model generated from Sionna [32]" (Sionna ray tracing, not 3GPP or DeepMIMO); the other settings are custom: p. 7 "the entries of G follow i.i.d. Gaussian distribution CN (0, 1)", p. 12 geometric mmWave model.
q2_support: p. 9: "when the neural network is trained on the Rayleigh fading model, which has a completely different characteristics as the testing data"; p. 8: "the neural network generalizes well in terms of different numbers of ping-pong rounds L".
q3_support: p. 7: "The proposed active sensing approach is compared with the following benchmarks" LMMSE+SVD, power iteration, summed power; p. 13: "The proposed active sensing framework is compared with the following benchmarks" perfect-CSI SVD, codebook power iteration, OMP+SVD, MTQR. All are non-learned; no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 15: "Table I shows the run time complexity comparison"; Table I on p. 15 lists the proposed method at "0.9079 (CPU)/ 0.0348 (GPU)" ms inference time.
q5_support: p. 1: "The source code for this paper is available at" the GitHub link github.com/taojiang-github/Active-Sensing-for-Reciprocal-MIMO-Channels.
notes: Page 1 shows the title and DOI 10.1109/TSP.2024.3412071. Area 3 and not 2: the learned method designs the pilot sensing beamformers and the final precoder and combiner, the main metrics are the log-det beamforming objective and the achievable rate, and no channel estimation error is reported (p. 1: "without explicit channel estimation"). q1 is marked 1 for the Sionna ray-tracing channel of Fig. 5 (p. 8), which is neither a 3GPP nor a DeepMIMO model and whose scene is not named in the text; reviewer to confirm. q3 is 0 because every benchmark in Figs. 3 and 8 is non-learned; the same authors' learned active sensing work [17] is discussed on p. 2 but not benchmarked. The GitHub URL is as rendered on p. 1; the text extraction drops the hyphen at the line break.
